metadata.description: Alfred H. Upham, signing as President, writes to Murray Sheehan in Gloucester, Massachusetts. He states that Miami University will be pleased to admit an unnamed prospective student as a freshman, notes the successful record of other boys from Thailand, and discusses holding a room after Freshman Week begins on September 14.
metadata.title: Letter to Murray Sheehan concerning a prospective student's admission, 8 September 1941
metadata.transcript:
[page 1]
September 8, 1941

Mr. [Mister] Murray Sheehan
Worcester 59
Gloucester, Massachusetts

Dear Murray:

Replying to your letter of September 6, I can assure you that we shall be pleased to admit Karon [illegible] to Miami University as a freshman.

While of course we know nothing of the University you mention in Bangkok or of its entrance examinations, the other boys from Thailand have made such a good record here that we do not hesitate.

Freshman Week begins with a convocation next Sunday evening, September 14, but we can hold a room for him a little longer if necessary. We are trying to squeeze him into one of the freshman dormitories.

Cordially yours,

President
